title: Indonesia & EU Forge Trade Ties Amidst Trump Tariffs
text:
With rising tariffs reshaping global commerce, both Indonesia and the EU are actively seeking new trade partnerships. This article dives into the strategic responses of Indonesia and the EU as thay navigate the new economic realities imposed by tariffs,with a focus on the ongoing negotiations for the Indonesia-EU Thorough Economic Partnership agreement (CEPA). Learn how this agreement could unlock critically important growth opportunities and foster trade diversification in the face of shifting global trade dynamics.
Indonesia, EU Eye Trade Pact as Trump Tariffs Reshape Global Commerce The Tariff Landscape: A New Era of trade Jakarta – Sweeping tariffs imposed by former US President Donald Trump have officially taken effect, prompting nations like Indonesia and members of the European Union to actively diversify their export markets.The initial 10 percent baseline tariff, implemented previously, has now been augmented by significantly higher import tax rates, reaching as high as 49 percent. These increased tariffs specifically target countries deemed by the Trump administration as engaging in unfair trade practices. Currently,imports originating from Indonesia face a reciprocal tariff of 32 percent,while the European Union is subject to a slightly lower rate of 20 percent.
Indonesia’s Strategic Response: negotiation and Diversification Rather than engaging in immediate retaliatory measures, Indonesia is pursuing a strategy centered on negotiation and the exploration of option markets. Airlangga Hartarto , a senior minister, stated that the Indonesia-EU Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) could serve as a crucial tool for accessing new markets in light of the recent US trade policies.Negotiations for the CEPA have been ongoing as July 2016, and according to Hartarto, the agreement is nearing completion, with only trade transparency issues remaining to be resolved.
“The US only accounts for 17 percent [of the world’s trade], and the rest comes from other countries. Mr. President [Prabowo Subianto] has instructed us to tap into that 83 percent global trade,”
Airlangga Hartarto, Senior Minister
Hartarto emphasized the importance of tapping into the larger global trade market, noting that the US accounts for only a fraction of worldwide commerce.
“The Indonesia-EU CEPA now only has one outstanding issue, namely on trade transparency. But I’m pretty sure we can get it done with the upcoming regulations to be announced by Mr. President,”
Airlangga Hartarto,Senior Minister
He expressed confidence that the remaining issues surrounding trade transparency within the CEPA could be resolved soon.
EU’s Perspective: Diversification and Continued Dialog The European Union is also actively pursuing diversification of its trade partnerships. French Trade Minister Laurent Saint-Martin ,during a press conference in Jakarta,addressed the potential for the CEPA negotiations to accelerate due to the US tariffs.Saint-martin was in Jakarta to prepare for French President Emmanuel Macron’s state visit to Indonesia, scheduled for late May.
“Generally speaking, the diversification of trade partnerships is indeed among Europe’s agenda. There is no doubt about that. … I’m confident that our EU commissioner will effectively continue the [CEPA] discussions with the Indonesian government,”
Laurent saint-Martin, French Trade Minister
Saint-Martin affirmed the EU’s commitment to diversifying trade partnerships and expressed optimism regarding the ongoing CEPA discussions.
Economic Implications and Trade Balance Data indicates that Europe represents a notable portion of global trade, accounting for 14 percent of the total. Hartarto highlighted the ample market potential within Europe for Indonesian goods, particularly footwear and apparel, perhaps surpassing opportunities available in the US. moreover, Indonesia maintains a trade surplus with the EU, amounting to nearly $4.5 billion in 2024, a notable increase from the $2.5 billion surplus recorded the previous year, according to the Trade Ministry.
Looking Ahead: The Path to Agreement Indonesia has set an ambitious goal to finalize the EU trade agreement talks within the first half of 2025. Achieving this woudl mark a significant step in strengthening economic ties between Indonesia and the European Union, providing both regions with new avenues for growth and trade diversification in a rapidly changing global economic landscape.
